messages:
sam: quick question — I have request_id=abc123 and need the raw log lines (not the pretty console view). Console search is timing out for me, any fast CLI/console trick?

anya: fastest path depends on whether you have a trace_id or only request_id. if you have trace_id -> open Traces -> find trace -> 'linked logs' icon. for request_id-only, try a direct indexed search in Logs first: `request_id:abc123` (filters -> query bar).

anya: if the console is slow, fallback to these quick CLI patterns I use:

```
# short time window via our CLI
rwctl logs --request-id abc123 --since 10m

# stream router logs from k8s and grep locally
stern router -n infra --since 15m | grep abc123

# kubectl one-liner (edge proxy pods)
kubectl logs -l app=edge-proxy -n infra --since=15m | grep abc123

# gcloud example for customers on GCP
gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.request_id="abc123"' --project=redwood-prod --limit 50
```

kevin: +1 to stern for quick hunts. two extra tips: 1) if you see nothing, check the header name the service sets (we historically used x-rw-req and x-request-id in different places). 2) sampling: traces may be sampled away — request log lines still exist but span link might be missing.

li: if you only have a trace id (trace: 1f2e3d4c), you can build the console link quickly: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/1f2e3d4c (replace host for region). also our Logs query that joins traces is `trace_id:1f2e3d4c OR request_id:abc123` — that returns either.

anya: when console indexing seems inconsistent, it usually means the ingestion shard for that time window is still catching up. check the 'Logs > Indexer health' dashboard (Ops -> Observability -> Logs -> Indexer). if it shows lag, use streaming grep against the pod logs as above.

observability-bot: FYI — log retention for `infra` index: 14 days hot, 30 days warm. Cold storage retrieval can take up to 2 hours.

sam: thanks — one wrinkle: I have only the response headers captured from a curl to prod, header shows `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01`. how do I map that to our trace_id search?

anya: extract the trace id from traceparent (the middle chunk). example: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-...` -> trace_id=4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736. then search `trace_id:4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736` in Logs/Traces.

kevin: also check the request router's x-forwarded-for/header rewrite. sometimes proxies drop or rewrite `traceparent` so you need to look at the ingress boundary logs. `kubectl logs -l app=ingress-nginx -n infra --since=15m | grep 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736`

li: if you hit an error like "no results" but you expect data, include a wider time range or try removing service filters. the console by default scopes to your last 1 hour and selected service. set time to 1h->12h and remove service filter.

sam: ran `rwctl logs --request-id abc123 --since 1h` and got something — thanks. last question: what's the canonical command I should paste in bug reports for others?

anya: I usually paste this short checklist (copyable):

```
# 1) get request_id from client or response header
# 2) try console quick search: request_id:<id> OR trace_id:<id>
# 3) if console slow, CLI stream: stern router -n infra --since 30m | grep <id>
# 4) fallback: kubectl logs -l app=edge-proxy -n infra --since=1h | grep <id>
# 5) if you have traceparent header: extract middle segment -> trace_id and search trace_id:<id>
# 6) check Logs Indexer dashboard for ingestion lag
```

observability-bot: If you open an incident with Observability, include `request_id`, `trace_id` (if available), time window, and the output of `rwctl diag indexer-status --json` to speed up triage.

sam: perfect — I'll paste that into the ticket. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
